title: kernel-routing-heuristics-and-pin-rollback-for-fine-grained-onboarding
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: When onboarding new model architectures (Mixture-of-Experts, Grouped-Query-Attention, and large MHA variants) we must publish a set of compiled kernel candidates and a pinned profile per model-version to guarantee stable latency and memory footprints for customers. Past rollouts exposed cases where a newly published kernel produced subtle tail-latency regressions or numerical quality drift for specific prompt shapes. This ticket designs and implements: 1) a kernel-routing heuristic that selects the optimal compiled kernel at request time based on model metadata, sequence-length distribution, and hardware class; 2) a metadata schema extension that attaches a pinned kernel-set and fallback policy to a model version in the model catalog; 3) an automated rollback mechanism (server-side and control-plane) that reverts active traffic to the previous pinned kernel-set if quality or SLO signals degrade after rollout; and 4) a publishing workflow for the model-onboarder to validate, certify, and expose compiled kernels and flags (quantization, kernel variant, compilation flags) to the console and API.
acceptance_criteria: Model-onboarder stores candidate compiled-kernel artifacts and exposes a pinned_kernel_set field on model-version metadata
Runtime selects kernel via heuristic with simulated workload achieving <=5% tail-latency regression vs baseline for 95th percentile
Automatic rollback triggers within 5 minutes of detecting sustained SLO violation tied to a model-version change
Console shows kernel-set lineage and allows manual pin/rollback and audit log entries for changes
Publishing workflow produces signed artifacts and a checksum for reproducible deployments
milestones: Design: kernel-routing decision graph and pin metadata schema — 2025-09-12
Benchmarks: compile candidates and perf matrix for MHA/GQA/MoE — 2025-09-26
Control-plane: pin storage, publish API, and rollback endpoint — 2025-10-03
Runtime: integration of routing heuristic and rollback signal handling — 2025-10-10
E2E: canary rollout with automatic rollback on perf regression — 2025-10-15
notes: Trade-offs: conservative pinning (fewer kernel variants) reduces maintenance but may miss opportunities for cost/latency wins; aggressive pinning requires stronger verification and increases artifact storage costs.
Quality signal sources: token-level quality deltas from evals (prompt set), P95/P99 latency, memory OOMs, and tail variance observed via tracing
Rollback policy: detect 3 consecutive 5-minute windows where P95 latency > baseline * 1.15 OR quality-regression > threshold => trigger rollback
Compatibility: fallback rules must include cross-model-version compatible kernel variants; fallback can choose next-best kernel or route to slower but more stable model variant
Storage: signed S3 artifact per compiled kernel + lightweight manifest with hardware tags (cuda-arch, cuDNN/ROCm versions, quantization profile)
implementation_steps: Add pinned_kernel_set and candidate_kernels array to model-onboarder manifest schema and API
Extend model catalog DB with kernel artifact metadata and checksums
Implement routing heuristic: inputs = model-version metadata, request seq-len, hardware-class, recent-profiled-latency; output = kernel-id
Add runtime hook to atomically switch kernel mapping for a model-version and emit an event to control-plane
Build control-plane rollback controller that listens to SLO alarms and performs atomic revert with audit log
Integrate canary rollout flagging in console: percentage-based rollout + automatic abort on violation
Create bench harness to run candidate kernels across seq-length histogram and record P50/P95/P99 and memory
Write certifier job that runs numeric checks on eval prompts and signs kernel artifacts
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: False-positive rollback due to noisy metrics — Mitigation: require sustained windows and correlate with quality evals before automated revert
Risk: Binary incompatibility across minor runtime versions — Mitigation: embed runtime-compat tags in manifest and block publish for mismatched runtimes
Risk: Storage blowup from many compiled candidates — Mitigation: retention policy + LRU eviction for older model-versions unless explicitly pinned
Risk: Latency cliffs on fallback — Mitigation: pre-warm and validate fallback kernels in staging canary prior to traffic shift
